vsm2.17:273.0:
SECTION C. THE WHEEL OF BECOMING
(I) THE WHEEL
vsm2.17:273.1:
Now, here at the end sorrow, etc., are stated. Consequently, the ignorance
stated at the beginning of the Wheel of Becoming thus, “With ignorance as condition there are formations,”
is established by the sorrow and so on. So it should accordingly be understood that:
vsm2.17:274.1:
But (1) how is ignorance established by sorrow, etc.? (2) How has this Wheel of Becoming no known beginning?
(3) How is there no maker or experiencer there? (4) How is it void with twelvefold voidness?
vsm2.17:275.1: 1. Sorrow, grief and despair are inseparable from ignorance; and lamentation is found in one who is deluded.
vsm2.17:275.2: So, firstly, when these are established, ignorance is established.
vsm2.17:275.3: Furthermore, “With the arising of cankers there is the arising of ignorance” (M I 54) is said,
vsm2.17:275.4: and with the arising of cankers these things beginning with sorrow come into being.
vsm2.17:276.1: Firstly, sorrow about separation from sense desires as object has its arising in the canker of sense desire,
vsm2.17:276.2:
according as it is said:

> If, desiring and lusting, his desires elude him,
> He suffers as though an arrow had pierced him (Sn 767),
vsm2.17:276.3: and according as it is said: “Sorrow springs from sense desires” (Dhp 215).
vsm2.17:277.1: And all these come about with the arising of the canker of views,
vsm2.17:277.2:
according as it is said: “In one who possesses the view ‘I am materiality,’ ‘my materiality,’ with the change
and transformation of materiality there arise sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair” (S III 3).
vsm2.17:278.1: And as with the arising of the canker of views, so also with the arising of the canker of becoming,
vsm2.17:278.2:
according as it is said: “Then whatever deities there are, long-lived, beautiful, blissful, long-resident in grand palaces,
when they hear the Perfect One’s teaching of the Dhamma, they feel fear, anxiety and a sense of urgency” (S III 85),
vsm2.17:278.3: as in the case of deities harassed by the fear of death on seeing the five signs.
vsm2.17:279.1: And as with the arising of the canker of becoming, so also with the canker of ignorance,
vsm2.17:279.2: according as it is said: “The fool, bhikkhus, experiences pain and grief here and now in three ways” (M III 163).
vsm2.17:279.3:
Now, these states come about with the arising of cankers, and so when they are established,
they establish the cankers which are the cause of ignorance.
vsm2.17:279.4: And when the cankers are established, ignorance is also established because it is present when its condition is present.
vsm2.17:279.5: This, in the first place, is how ignorance, etc., should be understood to be established by sorrow and so on.
vsm2.17:280.1:
2. But when ignorance is established since it is present when its condition is present, and when “with ignorance as condition there
are formations; with formations as condition, consciousness,” there is no end to the succession of cause with fruit in this way.
vsm2.17:280.2:
Consequently, the Wheel of Becoming with its twelve factors, revolving with the linking of cause and effect,
is established as having “no known beginning.”
vsm2.17:281.1:
This being so, are not the words “With ignorance as condition there are formations,”
as an exposition of a simple beginning, contradicted?—
vsm2.17:281.2: This is not an exposition of a simple beginning. It is an exposition of a basic state (see §107).
vsm2.17:281.3: For ignorance is the basic state for the three rounds (see §298).
vsm2.17:281.4:
It is owing to his seizing ignorance that the fool gets caught in the round of the remaining
defilements, in the rounds of kamma, etc.,
vsm2.17:281.5: just as it is owing to seizing a snake’s head that the arm gets caught in the coils of the rest of the snake’s body.
vsm2.17:281.6: But when the cutting off of ignorance is effected, he is liberated from them
vsm2.17:281.7: just as the arm caught in the coils is liberated when the snake’s head is cut off,
vsm2.17:281.8: according as it is said, “With the remainderless fading away and cessation of ignorance” (S II 1), and so on.
vsm2.17:281.9:
So this is an exposition of the basic state whereby there is bondage for him who grasps
it, and liberation for him who lets it go: it is not an exposition of a simple beginning.
vsm2.17:281.10: This is how the Wheel of Becoming should be understood to have no known beginning.
vsm2.17:282.1: 3. This Wheel of Becoming consists in the occurrence of formations, etc., with ignorance, etc., as the respective reasons.
vsm2.17:282.2:
Therefore it is devoid of a maker supplementary to that, such as a Brahmā conjectured thus, “Brahmā the Great,
the Highest, the Creator” (D I 18), to perform the function of maker of the round of rebirths;
vsm2.17:282.3:
and it is devoid of any self as an experiencer of pleasure and pain conceived thus,
“This self of mine that speaks and feels” (cf. M I 8).
vsm2.17:282.4: This is how it should be understood to be without any maker or experiencer.
vsm2.17:283.1:
4. However, ignorance—and likewise the factors consisting of formations, etc.—is void of lastingness since its nature is to rise
and fall, and it is void of beauty since it is defiled and causes defilement, and it is void of pleasure since it is oppressed
by rise and fall, and it is void of any selfhood susceptible to the wielding of power since it exists in dependence on conditions.
vsm2.17:283.2: And likewise the factors consisting of formations, etc.
vsm2.17:283.3: Or ignorance is neither self nor self’s nor in self nor possessed of self.
vsm2.17:283.4: And likewise the factors consisting of formations, etc.
vsm2.17:283.5: That is why this Wheel of Becoming should be understood thus, “Void with a twelvefold voidness.”
vsm2.17:284.1:
(II) THE THREE TIMES

After knowing this, again:
vsm2.17:284.2:
> Its roots are ignorance and craving;
> Its times are three as past and so on,
> To which there properly belong
> Two, eight, and two, from its twelve factors.
vsm2.17:285.1: The two things, ignorance and craving, should be understood as the root of this Wheel of Becoming.
vsm2.17:285.2: Of the derivation from the past, ignorance is the root and feeling the end.
vsm2.17:285.3: And of the continuation into the future, craving is the root and ageing-and-death the end. It is twofold in this way.
vsm2.17:286.1: Herein, the first applies to one whose temperament is false view, and the second to one whose temperament is craving.
vsm2.17:286.2:
For in the round of rebirths ignorance leads those whose temperament favours false
view, and craving those whose temperament favours craving.
vsm2.17:286.3:
Or the first has the purpose of eliminating the annihilation view because, by the evidence of the fruit,
it proves that there is no annihilation of the causes;
vsm2.17:286.4: and the second has the purpose of eliminating the eternity view because it proves the ageing and death of whatever has arisen.
vsm2.17:286.5: Or the first deals with the child in the womb because it illustrates successive occurrence of the faculties,
vsm2.17:286.6: and the second deals with one apparitionally born because of their simultaneous appearance.
vsm2.17:287.1: The past, the present and the future are its three times.
vsm2.17:287.2:
Of these, it should be understood that, according to what is given as such in the texts,
the two factors ignorance and formations belong to the past time,
vsm2.17:287.3: the eight beginning with consciousness belong to the present time,
vsm2.17:287.4: and the two, birth and ageing-and-death, belong to the future time.
vsm2.17:289.1: 1. Herein, between formations and rebirth-linking consciousness there is one link consisting of cause-fruit.
vsm2.17:289.2: Between feeling and craving there is one link consisting of fruit-cause.
vsm2.17:289.3:
And between becoming and birth there is one link consisting of cause-fruit. This is how it should
be understood that it has three links with cause, fruit, cause, as first parts.
vsm2.17:290.1: 2. But there are four sections, which are determined by the beginnings and ends of the links,
vsm2.17:290.2: that is to say, ignorance/formations is one section;
vsm2.17:290.5: and birth/ageing-and-death is the fourth. This is how it should be understood to have four different sections.
vsm2.17:291.1:
3. Then:

> (a) There were five causes in the past,
> (b) And now there is a fivefold fruit;
> (c) There are five causes now as well,
> (d) And in the future fivefold fruit.
vsm2.17:291.2: It is according to these twenty spokes called “qualities” that the words its spokes are twenty qualities should be understood.
vsm2.17:292.1:
(a) Herein, as regards the words There were five causes in the past, firstly only these two,
namely, ignorance and formations, are mentioned.
vsm2.17:292.2: But one who is ignorant hankers, and hankering, clings, and with his clinging as condition there is becoming;
vsm2.17:292.3: therefore craving, clinging and becoming are included as well.
vsm2.17:292.4:
Hence it is said: “In the previous kamma-process becoming, there is delusion, which is ignorance;
there is accumulation, which is formations; there is attachment, which is craving; there is embracing,
which is clinging; there is volition, which is becoming; thus these five things in the previous kamma-process
becoming are conditions for rebirth-linking here in the present becoming” (Paṭis I 52).
vsm2.17:293.1: Herein, In the previous kamma-process becoming means in kamma-process becoming done in the previous birth.
vsm2.17:293.2:
There is delusion, which is ignorance means that the delusion that there then was about suffering,
etc., deluded whereby the man did the kamma, was ignorance.
vsm2.17:293.3: There is accumulation, which is formations means the prior volitions arisen in one
vsm2.17:293.4: who prepares the things necessary for a gift during a month, perhaps, or a year after he has had the thought “I shall give a gift.”
vsm2.17:293.5: But it is the volitions of one who is actually placing the offerings in the recipients’ hands that are called “becoming.”
vsm2.17:293.6:
Or alternatively, it is the volition that is accumulation in six of the impulsions of a single
adverting that is called “formations,” and the seventh volition is called “becoming.”
vsm2.17:293.7: Or any kind of volition is called “becoming” and the accumulations associated therewith are called “formations.”
vsm2.17:293.8:
There is attachment, which is craving means that in one performing kamma, whatever attachment and aspiration
there is for its fruit as rebirth-process-becoming is called craving.
vsm2.17:293.9:
There is embracing, which is clinging means that the embracing, the grasping, the adherence,
which is a condition for kamma-process becoming and occurs thus, “By doing this I shall preserve, or I
shall cut off, sense desire in such and such a place,” is called clinging.
vsm2.17:293.10:
There is volition, which is becoming means the kind of volition stated already at the end of the sentence
dealing with accumulation is becoming. This is how the meaning should be understood.
vsm2.17:294.1: (b) And now there is a fivefold fruit (§291) means what is given in the text beginning with consciousness and ending with feeling,
vsm2.17:295.1:
Herein, there is rebirth-linking, which is consciousness means that it is what is called
“rebirth-linking” because it arises linking the next becoming that is consciousness.
vsm2.17:295.2:
There is descent into the womb, which is mentality-materiality means that it is what consists in the descent of the material
and immaterial states into a womb, their arrival and entry as it were, that is mentality-materiality.
vsm2.17:295.3: There is sensitivity, which is sense base: this is said of the five bases beginning with the eye.
vsm2.17:295.4:
There is what is touched, which is contact means that it is what is arisen when
an object is touched or in the touching of it, that is contact.
vsm2.17:295.5:
There is what is felt, which is feeling means that it is what is felt as results of kamma
that is arisen together with rebirth-linking consciousness, or with the contact that has the sixfold
base as its condition, that is feeling. Thus should the meaning be understood.
vsm2.17:296.1: (c) There are five causes now as well (§291) means craving, and so on. Craving, clinging and becoming are given in the text.
vsm2.17:296.2: But when becoming is included, the formations that precede it or that are associated with it are included too.
vsm2.17:296.3:
And by including craving and clinging, the ignorance associated with them,
deluded by which a man performs kamma, is included too. So they are five.
vsm2.17:296.4:
Hence it is said: “Here in the present becoming, with the maturing of the bases there is delusion, which is ignorance;
there is accumulation, which is formations; there is attachment, which is craving; there is embracing,
which is clinging; there is volition, which is becoming; thus these five things here in the present
kamma-process becoming are conditions for rebirth-linking in the future” (Paṭis I 52).
vsm2.17:296.5:
Herein, the words Here in the present becoming, with the maturing of the bases point out the delusion
existing at the time of the performance of the kamma in one whose bases have matured.
vsm2.17:297.1: (d) And in the future fivefold fruit: the five beginning with consciousness. These are expressed by the term “birth.”
vsm2.17:297.2: But “ageing-and-death” is the ageing and the death of these five themselves.
vsm2.17:297.3:
Hence it is said: “In the future there is rebirth-linking, which is consciousness; there is descent into the womb,
which is mentality-materiality; there is sensitivity, which is sense base; there is what is touched,
which is contact; there is what is felt, which is feeling; thus these five things in the future rebirth-process
becoming have their condition in kamma done here in the present becoming” (Paṭis I 52).
vsm2.17:297.4: So this Wheel of Becoming has twenty spokes with these qualities.
